newsitem.title: USA: Rauscher Pierce sees no conflict in seaport deals.
newsitem.headline: Rauscher Pierce sees no conflict in seaport deals.

text.p: Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc told Florida's Dade County finance committee Friday that it had not violated a rule that prohibits bond firms from charging issuers for MSRB underwriting assessments.

A letter sent to Committee Chairman Jimmy Morales alleged that Rauscher violated MRSB Rule A-13 by passing on to Palm Beach County, Fla., a $789 MSRB fee for the county's parks and recreation facilities bond issue in August.
Rauscher was senior manager for the Palm Beach County deal, and serves as financial adviser for Dade's seaport, water and sewer department and expressway authority.

A letter purportedly written by Leopoldo Guzman, president of the Miami bond underwriting firm Guzman & Co, accused Rauscher of the violation and urged Dade to dismiss the firm as its financial adviser. Guzman denied writing the letter. He said that it was a forgery and that he had asked the FBI to investigate.
But at a meeting Friday, Dade's finance committee sought assurances about the allegations raised in the letter.

Mike Abrams, first vice president at Rauscher, said the MSRB fee was included in an all-inclusive list of underwriter expenses for the deal but was not an additional fee charged by the firm to Palm Beach County.
He said Rauscher had consulted the MSRB and had received assurances from board officials that "it was not a violation."

Dade County Mayor Alex Penelas also questioned whether there was a violation of interest in Rauscher's acting as financial adviser for both the county seaport department and the Florida Ports Financing Commission.
A recent ports commission bond issue was used to fund grants to 14 Florida seaports, including a $44 million grant to the Port of Miami, which Dade County runs.
Abrams said there was no conflict of interest because the ports commission deal would have gone forward regardless who was its financial adviser or whether Dade participated.
Additionally, he said, the ports commission paid Rauscher a flat fee that was not based on the size of the issue or the number of participating ports.
"We categorically deny there's a conflict," Abrams said. "We didn't benefit from Dade County's participation."
Assistant County Manager David Morris and finance commitee chairman Jimmy Morales agreed that there was no conflict.
Dade has been especially skittish about potential conflicts of interest in light of an ongoing federal probe of allegations of kickbacks and corruption in Dade County and City of Miami bond deals.
